We need to identify misconceptions exhibited by student's code.

Problem: need O(n) time O(1) space two-sum on sorted array. Student code:

def has_pair(a, target):
    rest = list(a)
    for i in range(len(a)):
        need = target - a[i]
        if need in rest:
            j = rest.index(need)
            if j != i:
                return True
    return False

Issues: They copy list (rest) but then for each i they do "need in rest" which is linear scan O(n). Also rest.index is linear. So overall O(n^2). Also they are not using sorted property, they are scanning linearly. So misconception: "A linear membership test sits inside a loop, multiplying the cost." That's id "cx.membership-in-list". Also "The input carries an order the algorithm never exploits, so a logarithmic search is performed linearly." That's "search.linear-scan-when-ordered".
